name: widget_proxy
description: Does a cheap score predict the slow measurement?
https://w3id.org/claimcheck/ns#context:
One hundred samples in ten batches. Each has a cheap_score that takes a second
and a slow_measure_kJ that takes a day. The question is whether the cheap one can
stand in for the slow one, so that only the promising samples get the slow
measurement. coin_flip is a control: it is a seeded uniform draw and must not
correlate with anything.

The batch is the resampling unit. Ten of them is the smallest number that
separates the control from the signal here: an earlier version used four and the
noise came back "correlated" at r = 0.404, which was the design being
underpowered rather than a defect.

recordSet.name: measurements_csv_records

field.name: cheap_score
field.description: The fast proxy. Arbitrary units, which is what `1` means here.

field.name: slow_measure_kJ
field.description: The expensive measurement this project is trying to avoid making.

field.name: coin_flip
field.description: A seeded uniform draw. The control.

field.name: batch
field.description: Which batch a sample came from. The resampling unit: two samples in one batch are not independent of each other.

recordSet.description: One row per sample: the cheap score, the slow measurement and a control

https://w3id.org/claimcheck/ns#claims.why: claimed 0.9 lies OUTSIDE the 95% CI [0.912, 0.959] for r = 0.936, resampling 10 batch(s)
https://w3id.org/claimcheck/ns#claims.evidenceSource:
Claimed at 0.9 BEFORE looking at the data. If the interval excludes 0.9 the
prediction was wrong, in whichever direction. A verdict is about the prediction
and not about whether the proxy is any good.

https://w3id.org/claimcheck/ns#claims.why: claimed 0.0 lies within the 95% CI [-0.004, 0.303] for r = 0.157, resampling 10 batch(s)
https://w3id.org/claimcheck/ns#claims.evidenceSource:
Claimed at 0.0 and REQUIRED to hold. Noise must not correlate with the
measurement. If this is refuted the construction is broken and R1 cannot be
read, whichever way R1 went. It also shows how much room ten batches buys: the
width of this interval is the smallest correlation this design can tell from
nothing.
